introduction: Today we celebrate the Ascension of the Lord. Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus is taken up into heaven before the eyes of his apostles. He does not leave us orphans: he sends his disciples to proclaim the Good News to the whole world, promises the power of the Holy Spirit, and works with them. Let us lift our eyes to Christ in glory, and then go out as his witnesses.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ has ascended to the right hand of the Father, and he lives to intercede for us. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that, filled with the Holy Spirit, she may proclaim the Good News to the whole creation. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries, catechists and all who bring the Gospel to new places: that the Lord may work with them and confirm their words. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the unity of Christians: that we may keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick: that those who believe may lay hands on them in Christ's name and bring them his healing. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may not stand looking at the sky, but live as witnesses of the risen Lord where we are. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, your Son has gone before us into your glory. Fill us with the hope of following him, and give us the strength of your Spirit to be his witnesses. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Why do you stand looking into the sky?
reflection.body:
For forty days after Easter, Luke tells us, Jesus showed himself alive to his apostles "by many proofs" and spoke to them about God's Kingdom. Now the time has come for him to return to the Father.

The apostles still have their own plans. They ask, "Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?" Jesus does not answer their question. He gives them something better: "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth." Then "he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight."

They keep staring upward, until two men in white ask them, "You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky?" The Ascension is not a farewell to be mourned. Jesus will come again, and in the meantime there is work to do.

Mark gives us the mission in one sentence: "Go into all the world and preach the Good News to the whole creation." And he ends his Gospel with a promise kept: "They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them." Jesus has gone to the Father, but he has not gone away. He works with his Church.

Paul explains that the ascended Christ gives gifts to his people: apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds and teachers, all "to the building up of the body of Christ." Each of us has received a share of that grace. He also asks us to live "with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love."

The Ascension gives us two things: hope, because where Christ has gone we hope to follow; and a mission, because he has left his work in our hands. Between the Ascension and Pentecost, the Church prays for the coming of the Holy Spirit. Join that prayer this week, and ask the Spirit to show you where you are to be a witness.
